rationale: The construction is internally consistent and sign-coherent, but averaging the two conditioners already tested in the archive (turnover trend and gross-profit trend) is a consolidation whose outcome will almost mechanically land between the two existing results, making it a low-information variant rather than a new mechanism.

A defensible, narrowly-scoped test of persistence versus single-period measurement on the one archive signal where FMB and portfolio evidence diverged, though the three-year TS_SUM of DELTA(dltt) collapses to a simple three-year debt change and the design remains a close relative of DebtFinancedAccrualBuildup.

Inventory growth benchmarked against cost-of-sales growth is essentially the published inventory-growth / inventory-relative-to-sales anomaly (Thomas–Zhang, Belo–Lin) restated as a rank difference, and it drops the cross-theme conditioning that the archive was built to test.

The sign logic is coherent and the receivables/inventory decomposition is a fair question, but this reuses exactly the corner-product design whose FMB/alpha contradiction the same author diagnoses in the preceding proposal, so it is likely to reproduce that inconsistency with a different line item.

Expression, hypothesis and expected sign are consistent and using the cash stock as the external validator is the most genuinely distinct mechanism in this batch, though Δcash/at is heavily contaminated by financing and investment activity, so a negative result may be uninformative about the earnings-quality story.

Industry-demeaning is a mechanical re-ranking rather than new economics, but it is well justified here because asset turnover is structurally industry-determined, and it directly tests whether the archive's best result is a static industry bet the FF5 model cannot span.
